Subject: Discovery recap — tool calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Hi Samir / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 45-minute discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Summary / pain points you shared:
- Current inference routing is brittle when workflows need deterministic structured outputs (billing ingestion & downstream accounting jobs fail when JSON shape varies).
- You’re running a mix of internal microservices + managed endpoints (Finovo uses GCP Vertex for model training and a small fleet of in-house GPU workers for inference orchestration).
- Tool/function calling is critical for your agent workflows (lookups, DB writes, and external API calls) and you need guaranteed valid JSON from the model to avoid reconciliation issues.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 proof points and data residency controls are required before production launch.

Success criteria we captured:
1) Deterministic JSON output that matches a validated schema (errors flagged and rejected).
2) End-to-end agent workflow where model calls a function, we validate response, and call downstream services reliably.
3) Latency and cost targets: p99 < 600ms for common workflows, and per-call unit economics within your expected budget.
4) Security items: SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, and VPC options for sensitive workloads.

Technical notes / constraints you mentioned:
- You have strict schema validation in the billing pipeline — any deviation causes manual intervention.
- Versioned model rollouts are required; you may want canaries and automatic fallback.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll share a short tech checklist and example JSON schema that our Solutions team can prototype against.
- Marissa will coordinate a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your platform engineer and our Dev (Dev Patel) next week to walk the agent flow and schema validation tests.
- Samir / Maya: please share a representative prompt set, a sample of expected JSON schema(s), and any current failure examples you can anonymize.

Attachments: redwood-product-sheet.pdf (product overview)

Thanks —

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — good write-up. A few clarifications from our side: we absolutely need deterministic JSON output for billing flows (priority), and we expect schema validation to happen as a hard stop with error reporting back to the agent.

A couple of additional items:
- Our infra is mostly on GCP (Vertex for models, GKE for orchestration). We do have some on-prem batch jobs we need to protect.

Hi Samir / Maya —

Thanks for the quick reply and for sharing the tooling doc, Samir. I’m Dev (Solutions Engineer) — I’ll run the deep-dive and propose a short prototype plan. Below is a proposed agenda and a lean acceptance checklist so we’re all aligned before the technical call.

Proposed agenda (60m):
- 0–10m: intros + scope (what success looks like for this call)
- 10–30m: walkthrough of your existing agent flow and where you need function/tool calls to occur (examples from your doc)
- 30–45m: run through our deterministic JSON strategy: JSON schema enforcement, runtime validation, and failure modes (rollback, fallback, human-in-loop)
- 45–60m: next steps: prototype plan and data/sample requirements

Acceptance checklist (what demo / POC should prove):
- Model-produced output validated against a JSON Schema (we’ll use Draft 7 or newer) — failures get structured error objects and are not passed downstream.
- Agent function calls are instrumented and idempotent; we can replay with the same inputs and compare outputs.
- Deterministic formatting: template enforcement + post-generation validation to ensure fields and types match exactly.
- Observable audit trail: per-request trace id, model version, schema validation result, and error details available in the console/logs.

Prototype asks from your team (minimal):
1) Representative prompt set (5–10 prompts) and expected JSON schema(s).
2) A couple of anonymized failure examples where schema mismatch caused manual work.
3) A small test endpoint or test data we can call for integration (optional but helpful).

Scheduling: I’m available Tue 10–12 or Wed 14–17 PST. Jordan / Marissa — can you confirm a 60-min slot and send a calendar invite? Samir / Maya — which of the proposed times works?

I’ve attached a short SOW draft so procurement can have an early look; it’s editable and meant to accelerate timelines.

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf

Looking forward —
